symptom: A JSON payload with a member named `owner`, `changedDate`, `createdDate` or `changedBy` produces a project mxbuild refuses to build: **CE9524** "JSON element '(Object)/owner' has an invalid custom name 'Owner'. Custom name should start with a letter or underscore followed by either letters, digits or underscores."
cause: `create json structure` derives an ExposedName for every element (Studio Pro does too — 0 of 211 fixture elements have an empty one), and the derivation capitalises the initial. For a member Mendix reserves as a system attribute the derived name collides and Mendix rejects it. **The message is a red herring**: 'Owner' matches the character pattern it quotes perfectly; the real rule is the system-name collision. Isolated with a three-structure probe — `owner` and `changedDate` fail, `holder` passes
file: the JSON structure builder in `mdl/types/json_utils.go`; the reserved list already exists as `mendixSystemAttributeNames` in `mdl/executor/cmd_enumerations.go`
insight: `owner` is an ordinary member name in real REST payloads, so this is reachable from a plain `create json structure ... snippet`. Do not trust CE-message wording to name its own trigger — probe it: three one-line structures separated the system-name collision from the character pattern in one mx check. Found while building a runtime test app, not by any unit test. Filed separately
